Title: InfantAGI - An autonomous self improving python code writer and executer - Community - OpenAI Developer Community
URL: https://community.openai.com/t/infantagi-an-autonomous-self-improving-python-code-writer-and-executer/240242
Content: I would like to share with you my proof-of-concept Python program that uses OpenAI’s ChatGPT API to generate self-improving Python code. To use this program, you need to have an OpenAI API key, which you can enter in the code where it says “YOUR\_API\_KEY”. When you run the program, you will be prompted to give a task as input. The program will then refine the task by interacting with the first agent, who is responsible for this task. The refined task will be used as input for the second agent, who will create instructions for Python code to perform the task. If the task requires a web page, execution of the code may result in finding an information from web or performing a text to speech operation or plotting a graph, which regular chatgpt is not capable of. Then, run the program and follow the prompts to give a task as input, refine the task, create instructions for Python code, write the code, execute it, and give feedback to refine the instructions further.

Title: Building a Self-Healing AI Agent: How to Run Untrusted Code Safely Without Blowing Up Your Server - DEV Community
URL: https://dev.to/programmingcentral/building-a-self-healing-ai-agent-how-to-run-untrusted-code-safely-without-blowing-up-your-server-4859
Content: # Building a Self-Healing AI Agent: How to Run Untrusted Code Safely Without Blowing Up Your Server. Imagine you are building an autonomous AI agent. You give it a terminal tool, a file-writing tool, and the ability to execute Python scripts. In this deep dive, we will explore how the Hermes Agent framework (v0.13) solves this challenge using a multi-layered defense system, state-machine orchestration, and policy-based sandboxing. (The concepts and code demonstrated here are drawn from my ebook Hermes Agent, The Self-Evolving AI Workforce). The AI agent is the orchestrator. The tools are not just functions; they are the agent’s hands and eyes in the physical and digital world. The agent's core engine operates on a continuous loop of **perception** (receiving user input and tool results), **cognition** (the LLM call), and **action** (executing tool calls). This is the "containment vessel." It is not a single function, but a set of architectural patterns embedded in the execution of dangerous tools (like `terminal` and `execute_code`).

Title: The Self-Healing Code: Building an Autonomous Multi-Agent System That Fixes Itself | by Adi Insights and Innovations | Towards AI
URL: https://pub.towardsai.net/the-self-healing-code-building-an-autonomous-multi-agent-system-that-fixes-itself-b3bf641c52c5
Content: ## Towards AI. Join 100K+ AI practitioners on Towards AI Academy. # The Self-Healing Code: Building an Autonomous Multi-Agent System That Fixes Itself. Let’s build a swarm of agents that can detect errors, debate solutions, and rewrite their own source code autonomously. We are currently obsessed with “Chat with your Data.” But the future of Autonomous AI isn’t about conversation — it is about action and resilience. In the current landscape, if an AI agent hits a bug in its code or encounters an unexpected API error, it halts. But what if we could build a system that behaves like a biological immune system? Imagine a Multi-Agent System (MAS) where:. 1. An Executor Agent runs the code. 2. A Monitor Agent watches for errors. 3. A Doctor Agent diagnoses the bug and rewrites the code. Today, we are building exactly that. We are building an Autonomous Self-Healing Architecture. ## Published in Towards AI. ## Written by Adi Insights and Innovations.
